clue.text: Ostentation with provision of meals, or dash

parts.note: to make a splash is to show off; a splash is a showy display
board as in bed and board: meals provided

explanation.surface: A critic complains of showiness and lavish catering, or perhaps just haste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dash' is short for dashboard, the screen at the front of a carriage that keeps off mud.
explanation.definitionFit: A splashboard is the mud guard on a vehicle, also called a dashboard, which is clipped to dash.

clue.text: Scottish mount, first in Cairngorms, slender verges

indicators.note: verges are the edges, so these letters form the border placed around another

parts.note: slim means slender

indicators.note: 'first in' keeps only the first letter of 'Cairngorms'

parts.note: opening letter of Cairngorms

explanation.surface: A Scottish peak whose narrow edges hint at the Cairngorms range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mount' is a verb here, to climb; the Cairngorms are mountains in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Sclim is a Scots dialect verb meaning to climb, matching mount in the sense of ascend.

clue.text: Advertisements in favour of written work about love

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: abbreviation for manuscript
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Commercials supporting a written piece about romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Promos is the informal clipped plural of promotions, short adverts or trailers.

clue.text: PC of a kind left suitable work

parts.note: standard abbreviation
apt means fitting
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A computer has been left behind that would suit the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A laptop is a portable personal computer, one type of PC.

clue.text: Alto in earnest trilling pastoral cantata

indicators.note: trilling is a warbling, wavering sound, suggesting letters set quivering out of order

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for alto
taken as written

explanation.surface: An alto singer, trilling earnestly in a cantata of country life.
explanation.walkthrough: The alto is mixed in with the letters of earnest before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenata is an eighteenth-century dramatic cantata, often on a pastoral theme, related to the serenade.

clue.text: Farewell to Barcelona conveys bit of rhythmic music introducing scene (12, three words)

parts.note: conveys in the sense of carries or holds
a tala is a traditional rhythmic pattern in Indian music
a vista is a view or scene

explanation.surface: A goodbye to the Catalan city brings a snatch of rhythmic music as a prelude to a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barcelona' only signals Spanish; 'introducing' puts the first pieces before the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Hasta la vista is Spanish for see you later, a farewell a Spanish speaker would use.

clue.text: Part of speech amid four best broadcast? It's designed to minimize extremism

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside the other
broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is sown, so the letters are strewn about

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a verb is one of the parts of speech

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson on four top performers broadcasting, posing as an anti-extremism measure.
explanation.walkthrough: BERUFSVERBOT is German for professional ban: the West German rule barring political radicals from public-service jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: The ban kept people judged extremist out of public employment, a measure meant to curb radicalism.

clue.text: Rare enamel revealing gold letters

parts.note: chemical symbol for gold
mail is letters sent by post

explanation.surface: Uncommon enamel work shows gilded lettering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rare' is part of the definition, flagging a rarely used word, not an adjective for the enamel.
explanation.definitionFit: Aumail is a Spenserian verb meaning to enamel or ornament with colour, now very rarely used.

clue.text: There's nothing in grand lady forsaking steamer for jet

indicators.note: there is something within, so one piece sits inside another
forsaking means abandoning, so some letters are dropped

parts.note: a duchess is a lady of high rank
SS is steamship
zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A noble lady gives up the steamship for a jet plane, leaving nothing behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steamer' and 'jet' paint travel by sea and air, but jet means a spray of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A douche is a jet of water directed at the body, so jet in the spraying sense fits.

clue.text: Money owed on going into gum trees?

indicators.note: going into means entering, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the arar is the sandarac tree, which yields a gum resin
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: Money due gets stuck up among the gum trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gum trees' suggests eucalyptus, but arars are North African conifers giving sandarac gum.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrears are payments that are overdue, debts still owed.

clue.text: Infatuation to follow clubs, a longing

indicators.note: to follow means coming after, so one piece is placed after the other

parts.note: abbreviation for the card suit
a rave is a craze or infatuation

explanation.surface: An obsession with joining clubs, a yearning to belong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a longing' looks like part of the surface tail but is the definition, crave used as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, crave means a strong desire or yearning, an older usage given in Chambers.

clue.text: Fashioned rotunda? Note one neglected, Late Perpendicular

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped anew, so the letters are reworked
neglected means left out, so the named letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
N is an abbreviation for note
a means one

explanation.surface: An architect notes a remodelled rotunda, built in the late Perpendicular style.
explanation.walkthrough: Perpendicular is the last phase of English Gothic architecture; its final flowering is called Tudor.
explanation.definitionFit: Tudor architecture is the late stage of the Perpendicular Gothic style in England, so the style name fits.

clue.text: Lander in Sydney, name admitted by local informer?

indicators.note: admitted by means let inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: in Australian slang a dog is an informer, local to Sydney
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A newcomer landing in Sydney is reported by a neighbourhood snitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lander' is a punch that lands, not an arriving traveller; 'local' points to Australian usage.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang a dong is a heavy blow, the kind of punch that connects.

clue.text: See individual scratching on desktop supports

parts.note: lo means look, see

indicators.note: scratching means striking out, so some letters are removed

parts.note: a person is an individual
taken as written

explanation.surface: Watch someone scratching at the surface of a desk.
explanation.walkthrough: Lopers are the sliding rails that pull out to hold up the flap of a bureau desk.
explanation.definitionFit: Lopers are the pull-out bearers that support the hinged writing surface of a bureau.

clue.text: Gossip displaying disposition right for husband

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter swaps in for another

parts.note: humour is temperament, mood
standard abbreviation
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Tittle-tattle reveals whether a wife's mood suits her husband.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumour is unverified talk passed around, which is gossip.

clue.text: Favourite clue spoilt if once included in it is peevishness

parts.note: a pet is a favourite

indicators.note: included in means placed within, so one piece goes inside
spoilt means damaged, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
an is an archaic word for if

explanation.surface: A solver grumbles that a favourite clue is ruined by an extra word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to the jumbled clue, which takes the old word for if inside it.

clue.text: It's fine in SA — I'll join Dutch uncle retiring there

indicators.note: join means attach, so the pieces are set side by side

parts.note: oom is Dutch and Afrikaans for uncle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A South African says all is well once their stern Dutch uncle has gone to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: SA is South Africa, where Afrikaans, descended from Dutch, gives both words. A Dutch uncle is also a stern adviser, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: Mooi is South African slang from Afrikaans meaning pleasing, nice, fine.

clue.text: Crowned sovereign to the French, king mostly worried

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a sovereign is a pound coin, and L stands for pound
au is French for to the
R for rex, king
eaten up, consumed with worry

explanation.surface: A crowned monarch speaking to the French while the king frets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crowned sovereign' reads as one phrase, but crowned is the definition and the sovereign is a gold coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Laureate means crowned with laurel as an honour, the original sense behind poet laureate.

clue.text: Observation I inserted in error returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word reads backwards
inserted in means put inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or error
taken as written

explanation.surface: A proofreader notes an I slipped in by mistake and sent back.
explanation.definitionFit: Espial is the act of spying or catching sight, hence observation.

clue.text: Geological period wherein you'll find seabird, one inhabiting Pyrenean area

indicators.note: wherein you will find means inside which something sits

parts.note: an era is a division of geological time
the skua is a predatory gull-like seabird

explanation.walkthrough: Eskuara is the Basque language; the Basque country straddles the western Pyrenees.
explanation.definitionFit: Eskuara is a variant of Euskara, the Basque tongue, spoken by the people of the western Pyrenees.

clue.text: One dealing in dyes etc changes back to front

indicators.note: back to front means the rear letter is carried round to the start

parts.note: alters means changes

explanation.surface: A dye merchant reshuffles their stock from back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: Salter is short for drysalter, an old trade in dyes, gums and chemicals as well as salted goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A salter, or drysalter, was a dealer in dyes, chemicals and preserved foods.

clue.text: A container in Adelaide's place displays this WI evergreen

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: Adelaide is the capital of South Australia, SA

explanation.surface: A pot in an Adelaide garden shows off a tropical evergreen.
explanation.walkthrough: WI is the West Indies.
explanation.definitionFit: The sapota is a tropical American and West Indian evergreen tree, the sapodilla, bearing edible fruit.

clue.text: Stroll, not heading for exciting experience as of old

indicators.note: not heading means without its first letter, which is dropped

parts.note: saunter means stroll

clue.text: Those making choice re post to be broadcast

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: Endlessly sick? Whimper about it, calling for tablet

clue.text: Strong drink? 9 and, in short, I'll be sozzled!

parts.note: the number written as a word

explanation.walkthrough: '9' is not a cross-reference to 9-down; it is just the number. The setter's I stands for Azed, which is then shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: Enzian is a German schnapps distilled from gentian roots, a potent spirit.

clue.text: Drove to Scotland for something to wear men'll be out of

taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Gart is the Scots past tense of gar, to make or compel, as drove means forced along.

clue.text: It was used to treat malaria, contributing to skin allergy

parts.note: letters running across the two words

clue.text: Sailor's left … his unnamed starting point?

explanation.definitionFit: Aport means on or towards the port side, which is the left side of a vessel facing forward.

clue.text: I'll be enthralled by nude tart dancing with nothing on

clue.text: Member of family, one Tantalus initially cursed terribly (all in it)

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: terribly means in a dreadful way, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the inner four letters, to be shuffled

clue.text: Tempestuous event? It makes one sack auditor regularly failing

clue.text: Changing liras to …? This is likewise

definitions.note: stands for a currency like the lira just named

explanation.definitionFit: The tolar was Slovenia's currency until 2007, a monetary unit as the lira was Italy's.

clue.text: Fresh declaration? Old team put in ran test chaotically
